      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Async legacy writes inherit request context and will be canceled prematurely",
      "body": "The goroutines started for legacy writes (Create line 51, Delete line 110, Update line 135, DeleteCollection line 163) use the same `ctx` that was derived from the incoming HTTP request. When the HTTP handler returns, the request context is canceled by the server, causing the legacy write to be aborted before it completes. This defeats the purpose of the asynchronous safe write and will likely cause legacy data loss. Use a context detached from the request (e.g., `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or a new background context) for these goroutines."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "line": 139,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Legacy Update reuses the same UpdatedObjectInfo causing a second invocation",
      "body": "The legacy update goroutine passes the same `objInfo` that was already used by `d.Storage.Update`. This causes `objInfo.UpdatedObject` to be invoked a second time, possibly against a different old object (the legacy store's current state), leading to incorrect data or side effects. The previous implementation wrapped the already updated object to reuse it for legacy; that behavior was lost. This can produce updates inconsistent with what was written to unified storage."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "line": 45,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Wrong metric function used on storage error in Create",
      "body": "When `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`. This records the storage failure as a legacy operation and pollutes the legacy latency metrics, making monitoring misleading. Similar mislabels occur in Update (line 129) and in the DeleteCollection goroutine (line 166)."
    },
    {

      "line": 106,
      "severity": "medium",

      "title": "Storage duration metric for Delete uses object name as kind",
      "body": "After a successful storage delete, the call `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the object `name` as the `kind` argument. The metric label will be incorrectly populated with resource names instead of resource kinds, breaking dashboard queries and alerts based on the `kind` label."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go",
      "line": 97,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "style",
      "title": "Delete uses wrong logger when updating context",
      "body": "In `Delete`, the code sets `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of using the per-call `log` variable that includes method, name, and kind. As a result, subsequent log entries from this context will lack the per-request fields, reducing log usefulness."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go",
      "line": 31,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Mode 3 unit tests do not wait for or assert async legacy writes",
      "body": "The tests set up legacy store mocks but never call `m.AssertExpectations(t)` nor synchronize with the goroutines performing the legacy writes. The async operations may still be running when the test ends, and failures in legacy writes are not detected. This leaves the mode 3 legacy write path essentially untested. The tests should use a channel or wait group to ensure the goroutine completes and then verify the legacy mock was called and metrics recorded correctly."
    },
    {
      "file": "pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go",
      "line": 132,
      "severity": "medium",

      "title": "Integration tests for mode 3 may be flaky due to asynchronous legacy writes",
      "body": "The `doPlaylistTests` function checks that legacy API endpoints reflect changes made through the Kubernetes API immediately after operations. In mode 3, legacy writes are asynchronous and not awaited, so the legacy API may not have the latest data when the test queries it. This can cause intermittent failures in the newly added mode 3 test cases. The tests need a synchronization mechanism (or the implementation must guarantee completion before returning) to be reliable."
    }

findings.title: Async legacy writes inherit request context and will be canceled prematurely
findings.body: The goroutines started for legacy writes (Create line 51, Delete line 110, Update line 135, DeleteCollection line 163) use the same `ctx` that was derived from the incoming HTTP request. When the HTTP handler returns, the request context is canceled by the server, causing the legacy write to be aborted before it completes. This defeats the purpose of the asynchronous safe write and will likely cause legacy data loss. Use a context detached from the request (e.g., `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` or a new background context) for these goroutines.

findings.title: Legacy Update reuses the same UpdatedObjectInfo causing a second invocation
findings.body: The legacy update goroutine passes the same `objInfo` that was already used by `d.Storage.Update`. This causes `objInfo.UpdatedObject` to be invoked a second time, possibly against a different old object (the legacy store's current state), leading to incorrect data or side effects. The previous implementation wrapped the already updated object to reuse it for legacy; that behavior was lost. This can produce updates inconsistent with what was written to unified storage.

findings.title: Wrong metric function used on storage error in Create
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`. This records the storage failure as a legacy operation and pollutes the legacy latency metrics, making monitoring misleading. Similar mislabels occur in Update (line 129) and in the DeleteCollection goroutine (line 166).

findings.title: Storage duration metric for Delete uses object name as kind
findings.body: After a successful storage delete, the call `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the object `name` as the `kind` argument. The metric label will be incorrectly populated with resource names instead of resource kinds, breaking dashboard queries and alerts based on the `kind` label.

findings.title: Delete uses wrong logger when updating context
findings.body: In `Delete`, the code sets `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` instead of using the per-call `log` variable that includes method, name, and kind. As a result, subsequent log entries from this context will lack the per-request fields, reducing log usefulness.

findings.title: Mode 3 unit tests do not wait for or assert async legacy writes
findings.body: The tests set up legacy store mocks but never call `m.AssertExpectations(t)` nor synchronize with the goroutines performing the legacy writes. The async operations may still be running when the test ends, and failures in legacy writes are not detected. This leaves the mode 3 legacy write path essentially untested. The tests should use a channel or wait group to ensure the goroutine completes and then verify the legacy mock was called and metrics recorded correctly.

findings.title: Integration tests for mode 3 may be flaky due to asynchronous legacy writes
findings.body: The `doPlaylistTests` function checks that legacy API endpoints reflect changes made through the Kubernetes API immediately after operations. In mode 3, legacy writes are asynchronous and not awaited, so the legacy API may not have the latest data when the test queries it. This can cause intermittent failures in the newly added mode 3 test cases. The tests need a synchronization mechanism (or the implementation must guarantee completion before returning) to be reliable.
